Construction NVQ assessor brief in system prompt

When on, each request sends a bundled UK construction NVQ/IQA-oriented brief to your server (static text in the app). It supports planning and mapping—it does not replace AO specs or professional judgement. Real “learning” from your cases needs your server (e.g. retrieval over your notes), not on-device LLM training.

When on, the app logs subject line plus message sizes only (no full chat text by default), shows summaries on the home screen, and adds a short observation block to the assistant system prompt so replies can streamline recurring workflows. Turn off for maximum privacy.

Turn this on to let Tab ML Box listen for construction / NVQ-related words that appear on screen in other apps. Nothing is uploaded: only local keyword checks. You must also enable the accessibility service in Android settings. The app then asks whether to enable observation learning for the assistant.
Accessibility service for Tab ML Box:
Notices construction / NVQ-related on-screen text and offers to turn on observation learning.

When Tab ML Box’s “Look for NVQ-related screen text” is on, this service reads visible text from the current window to match a short list of UK construction qualification phrases. It does not store screen contents. It may show a notification or in-app prompt so you can choose whether Tab ML Box should observe and learn (assistant session logging + NVQ brief). Disable this in Accessibility settings anytime.

Each message includes this subject so the assistant can tailor library and model advice.
Turn on “Allow HTTPS downloads” on the main screen, then return here.

You can use Cali in two ways.

1) On this tablet: turn on “Run LLM on this tablet” in settings, download the starter Llama 3.2 GGUF (large download; needs “Allow HTTPS downloads” once), and pick the matching “Chat template” for any model you replace the file with.

2) Remote server: leave that off and set “Assistant base URL” to an OpenAI-compatible POST /v1/chat/completions service (Ollama, vLLM, LiteLLM, etc.). Set “Model name” to the id your server expects. For streaming tokens in the chat bubble, your server should honour `stream: true` (SSE or NDJSON), otherwise Cali falls back to a normal JSON reply.

“Bearer token” is optional for remote mode if your server does not check Authorization.

Release builds require https:// for remote URLs. Debug builds also allow http:// for local development.

Optional “Cali” wake word: on the main Tab ML Box screen, download the small English Vosk model (same as offline speech), then turn on “Listen for wake word”. Cali opens chat with the mic when it hears “Cali” or similar. Listens in the foreground with a notification.

This app cannot edit Gradle files on the device. It can suggest dependency lines for you to paste in Android Studio. It can suggest installing a .tflite file only when you or your server provides a real https:// link in the agreed format.

No suggested .tflite in the last reply.
Messages go only to your configured HTTPS server. The assistant cannot merge Gradle dependencies inside the app.

Open “Your server settings” and set your assistant base URL. The app only talks to that OpenAI-compatible server — your custom LLM or proxy. Release builds require https://. Debug builds also accept http:// for local setups (e.g. Ollama on a desktop).
That URL is not allowed: use https://, or in debug builds only you may use http:// for a local LLM.
